purpose: Enumerate every language-runtime dependency manifest in this repository (requirements.txt, pyproject.toml/uv.lock, package.json/pnpm-lock.yaml, Cargo.toml/Cargo.lock), check each for a hash-pinned lockfile and a Dependabot updater entry for its package ecosystem, and record which runtimes are unlocked and/or unowned.
preregistered: manifests/stack.json's components[] are installed CLI tools, not in-repository language runtimes with dependency manifests, so the actual runtime surface is the concrete manifest files found by repository walk. If every found manifest has both a hash-pinned lockfile and a matching .github/dependabot.yml package-ecosystem entry, that would refute the gap (locking and update ownership are established). If any manifest lacks a lockfile or lacks an assigned updater, that supports the gap's claim and the specific unlocked/unowned runtimes are recorded by name, settling this (non-time-gated) half of gap 12 either way. FIX ROUND CORRECTION (2026-09-23): the 'CLI tools, not runtimes' framing for manifests/stack.json is wrong -- its components[] include externally-installed Python/runtime packages (pandas, skfolio, alpaca-py, edgartools, exchange-calendars, vllm, headroom, llama-cpp, nextjs etc.), not only CLI tools, and this script's in-repository-manifest walk does not audit their lock/update status at all. 'Across every runtime' is therefore not established; settles_gap is corrected to partially. Separately, the committed script's requirements*.txt glob was found to also match blueprints/gap-wave2-20260923/grype-known-cve-fixture/requirements.txt (a check fixture added by a sibling unit, not a real runtime manifest), producing 5 manifests instead of the originally recorded 4; the script is corrected here to exclude the blueprints/gap-wave2-20260923/ check-tooling subtree, restoring the original 4-manifest, byte-identical result (verified by rerunning the corrected script and comparing sha256 to the originally retained output). No check was re-run to fish for a different substantive outcome; this is a script-scoping fix that reproduces the original recorded numbers.

result: Found 4 dependency manifests in the repository: blueprints/convergence-practice/application-delivery/pyproject.toml (has uv.lock, hash-pinned, 212 `hash =` entries), blueprints/convergence-practice/application-delivery/package.json (has pnpm-lock.yaml, `integrity:` hash-pinned), blueprints/us-equities/adaptive-paper/requirements.txt (plain `==` pins, zero `--hash` entries, no lockfile), blueprints/us-equities/workers/requirements.txt (plain `==` pins, zero `--hash` entries, no lockfile). .github/dependabot.yml's only package-ecosystem entry is `github-actions`; it has no `pip`, `npm` or `uv` entries at all. So 2 of 4 in-repository manifests have a hash-pinned lockfile (application-delivery's Python and Node runtimes) and 2 do not (both requirements.txt files in the us-equities blueprints), while 0 of 4 have any assigned Dependabot updater for their actual package ecosystem -- Dependabot in this repository currently updates only GitHub Actions pins, never Python/npm dependencies. FIX ROUND CORRECTION: this enumeration covers in-repository dependency manifests only. manifests/stack.json's components[] additionally list externally-installed Python/runtime packages actually used by this stack (pandas 3.0.6, skfolio 1.2.9, alpaca-py 0.44.0, edgartools 5.58.0, exchange-calendars 4.13.2, vllm 0.25.0, headroom, llama-cpp, nextjs, among 69 components) whose own lock/update status (e.g. whether their installing environment is pinned by hash, and who updates them) was not audited here at all -- the original claim that this script covers 'every runtime' was wrong; it covers only the 4 in-repository application manifests.

verdict_impact.explanation: For the 4 in-repository manifests actually audited, complete dependency locking is not established (2 of 4 unlocked) and ongoing update ownership is not established for any of them (0 of 4 have a Dependabot ecosystem entry) -- this refutes any incumbent claim that dependency locking and update ownership are already established across the repository's runtimes. It is recorded as refutes_incumbent, not supports_incumbent: the gap's premise (that this is unestablished) is what this check confirms, so the check result argues against treating the incumbent posture as already adequate. The check does not cover manifests/stack.json's externally-installed runtime packages, so it settles only the in-repository-manifest half of gap 12, hence settles_gap is partially, not true.

limitations: Scoped to in-repository dependency manifests only; does not audit manifests/stack.json's externally-installed runtime/library components (pandas, skfolio, alpaca-py, edgartools, exchange-calendars, vllm, headroom, llama-cpp, nextjs and others among its 69 components) at all -- their lock/pin status and update ownership are unaudited by this check, so 'across every runtime' is not established, only 'across every in-repository application manifest'.

Does not check whether uv.lock/pnpm-lock.yaml are actually enforced in CI (e.g. `uv sync --locked` / `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`); only that the lockfiles exist and contain hash/integrity fields.

Dependabot's actual scheduled-update behavior (weekly timing, grouped minor/patch PRs) remains unobserved and is explicitly out of scope here (gap 4, time-gated, not part of this unit's assigned gaps).
This is a static Python walk over repository files (glob + text search), not execution of an external native tool; evidence_class is local_integration, not native_proven.

The script's requirements*.txt glob previously also matched a sibling unit's check fixture (blueprints/gap-wave2-20260923/grype-known-cve-fixture/requirements.txt), producing a 5-manifest result that did not match this receipt's claims. The script now excludes the blueprints/gap-wave2-20260923/ check-tooling subtree; this was verified to reproduce the original 4-manifest output byte-for-byte (same sha256) rather than changing the substantive result.
